76660.subject: Beyond The AMM
76660.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Hi everyone. Ahead of today's FOMC decision, markets remain in wait-and-see mode as rate hike expectations continue to weigh on risk assets. We also take a closer look at one of the biggest structural shifts in onchain markets: the rapid rise of RFQ trading in tokenized equities. While the data suggests RFQs are taking the lead, the reality is more nuanced than the headline numbers imply.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Across the majors, this is a de-risking week with nothing green. BTC leads the drawdown, down -4.2%, followed by the Nasdaq at -4.1% and gold at -1.9%. The S&P 500 has held up best, falling just -0.7%. The cause is this afternoon's FOMC decision: hike odds have climbed back to roughly 35% from 10.7% on July 15, undoing the relief the softest consumer price index (CPI) print of 2026 delivered two weeks ago. BTC is still up 7.1% on the month compared with a -4.8% decline for the Nasdaq, so this is a give-back inside a larger move rather than a new leg lower.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dd6038d7-ee0d-4c6b-b55e-914d123eaa39/image.png?t=1785332895)
Caption: 

Tuesday itself was mixed, with DEXs the clear standout at 4.2% while BTC was little changed, gaining 0.2%. AI followed at 3.7%, crypto equities 3.4%, and Ethereum Eco 3.0%; Solana Eco was the worst of the tape at -3.5%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/df656a1d-ed2e-4175-8c11-91688e14185b/image.png?t=1785332895)
Caption: 

Four sectors are green on the week and three of them are Ethereum-related: Ethereum Eco (+5.7%), Lending (+5.7%), and DEXs (+3.5%) were positive, with Bittensor Eco (+0.9%) the outlier against AI at -3.6%. The listed-crypto complex took the worst of it as crypto miners fell -13.2%, crypto equities -8.2%, and the 2025 equity cohort -8.1%, all trading as high-beta equity against the NASDAQ's -4.1%. Privacy unwound its upgrade trade at -9.1% as ZEC fell -12.0% once Ironwood activated Tuesday at block 3,428,143, though it holds +24.3% on the month.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4d503625-5140-4ee8-ad98-b7c8409b7348/image.png?t=1785332896)
Caption:

The Automation Divide: Why "Good Enough" AI No Longer Wins
 Enterprise Deals
76657.body:
Ment Tech | Meant To Innovate

Автор: Ment Tech Labs


Автор: Ment Tech Labs

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/automation-divide-why-good-enough-ai-longer-wins-enterprise-ccw7f?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BKzzOcZlOTTuPDQhpwMqnBA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3MrUarozdq2co1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~ms62rvks~uv-null-null&eid=fz96fz-ms62rvks-uv
  
A chatbot used to impress a board. Now it gets a shrug. The question changed. Leaders don't ask "can we automate this?" anymore. They ask: can this system run inside how we actually work our approvals, our compliance checks, our legacy tools, our edge cases? That's a harder question, and it's why AI automation services have gone from side project to core budget line. The Market, In Numbers These aren't hype numbers. They're a signal that automation has moved from pilot project to infrastructure. Why Copy-Paste Automation Keeps Failing ? Most companies didn't fail because the model was weak. They failed because they installed a generic tool and expected it to behave like a custom AI automation service built for their business. A logistics approval chain looks nothing like a hospital intake form. A finance reconciliation process shares no rules with a retailer's inventory sync. Yet most businesses install the same platform, flip the same switches, and expect the same lift everyone else got. Generic AI Tool vs. Purpose-Built AI Automation Service That gap generic tool vs. purpose-built AI and automation service is the biggest difference between companies that automate profitably and companies that automate expensively. Where the Returns Are Actually Showing Up ? Finance teams closing books in days, not weeks reconciliation runs overnight Support teams resolving most routine tickets before a human sees them Operations teams alerted the moment a shipment, invoice, or order breaks pattern Sales teams working leads that are pre-qualified and pre-scored before the first call None of this came from installing "AI" in the abstract. It came from ai workflow automation services mapped to one specific, expensive, recurring bottleneck then wired directly into the tools teams already use. The Agency Question Companies Are Finally Asking Fewer companies are trying to build everything in-house. Fewer are settling for a rigid SaaS template either. More are looking for an ai automation agency services partner that can sit between the raw model and the messy reality of the business.
